did_you_know.text: Did you know? At the beginning of the list of Benjamin’s sons, five sons are named in birth order: Bela, the firstborn; Ashbel, the second; Aharah, the third; Nohah, the fourth; and Rapha, the fifth.
Did you know? The sons of Ehud are described as heads of the families of the inhabitants of Geba, and the passage says that they were deported to Manahath.
Did you know? Shaharaim fathered sons in the land of Moab through the women mentioned in the verse: Hushim and Baara.
Did you know? Elpaal is described not only as the father of a large family, but also as the builder of Ono, Lod, and its surrounding villages.
Did you know? Beriah and Shema are mentioned as heads of the families of the inhabitants of Aijalon, and the passage credits them with driving out the inhabitants of Gath.
Did you know? The list emphasizes that many of these family heads lived in Jerusalem.
Did you know? At the head of the family of Gibeon, Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, and his wife Maacah are mentioned; their sons and descendants are then listed.
Did you know? A central genealogy in the chapter runs from Ner to Kish, from Kish to Saul, and from Saul to Jonathan and his three other sons: Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.
Did you know? Merib-Baal, Jonathan’s son, fathered Micah; thus the list continues Jonathan’s genealogy into later generations.
Did you know? The sons of Ulam are described as mighty warriors and skilled archers, and as having a large family: 150 sons and grandsons.
